title: Register, translation choices and editorial revision

questions.prompt: Formal interpretation of a translated Francophone migration testimony: which formulation best fits an academic report?
choices: Les résultats appellent une interprétation prudente.
Ces chiffres, c'est du grand n'importe quoi.
C'est évident pour tout le monde.
questions.explanation: A measured, impersonal tone suits academic reporting.

questions.prompt: Disputed historical interpretation of a migration policy: choose a neutral attribution that does not assert scholarly consensus.
choices: La réforme a certainement échoué parce que je le dis.
Tous les historiens savent forcément la vérité.
Selon l'auteur, la réforme aurait échoué.
questions.explanation: Selon l'auteur attributes the position rather than asserting consensus.

questions.prompt: Interpreting a fictional family's departure: which English translation preserves the uncertainty of « Il aurait quitté la ville »?
choices: He was expected to leave the city under the proposed relocation plan.
He reportedly left the city.
He would leave the city if the conditions changed.
questions.explanation: Here the isolated past conditional may signal an unconfirmed report; 'reportedly' expresses that evidentiary reading without imposing a condition not present.

questions.prompt: Unverified migration-archive metadata: which French expression introduces an explicit qualification?
choices: Sous réserve de vérification,
Sans aucune nuance possible,
De façon incontestable,
questions.explanation: Sous réserve de vérification signals that a claim needs confirmation.

questions.prompt: Editing an informal note about a migrant's personal documents: which formal French revision of « Ce document dit plein de trucs » is most appropriate?
choices: Ce document raconte un tas de machins.
Ce document balance des trucs.
Ce document présente plusieurs éléments.
questions.explanation: Présente plusieurs éléments preserves the nonspecific sense of plein de trucs while removing the informal expression and using an appropriate formal register.

questions.prompt: A bilingual migration-exhibit translation note: which phrase transparently identifies the translator's intervention?
choices: Traduction révisée par l'éditeur, sans indication des nuances modifiées.
Traduction proposée par l'éditeur; nuance expliquée en note.
Traduction établie d'après le texte source, sans préciser l'intervention éditoriale.
questions.explanation: The chosen note both identifies the editorial translator and explains a specific change in nuance; the others disclose less.

questions.prompt: In a scholarly exhibit on displacement, which construction uses a quotation with necessary interpretive context?
choices: L'historienne écrit « transition », terme qu'elle définit ensuite.
L'historienne écrit « transition », preuve de tous les faits.
Le mot « transition » démontre sans contexte la causalité.
questions.explanation: A quotation needs its authorial context and interpretation.

questions.prompt: Fictional dated migrant-arrival record with disputed causes: which formulation separates a documented date from interpretation?
choices: La date est connue, donc toutes les causes sont certaines.
Une date attestée rend inutile toute enquête.
La date est attestée; ses causes restent discutées.
questions.explanation: Documented chronology does not settle contested causation.

questions.prompt: Comparing conflicting migration memoir accounts: which English connector best translates « pourtant » to introduce a counterpoint?
choices: therefore
however
because
questions.explanation: Pourtant marks contrast or an unexpected counterpoint.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'éditeur a modernisé l'orthographe sans le signaler ». What is the issue?
choices: Readers may mistake edited spelling for the original.
The document necessarily contains no useful history.
No editorial choice was made.
questions.explanation: Unsignaled modernization obscures features of the source text.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le mot république est traduit par state sans commentaire ». What should be checked?
choices: Whether all political nouns have one exact equivalent.
Whether translation has no interpretive choices.
Whether political meaning was altered in context.
questions.explanation: An institutional term may lose its specific nuance in translation.

questions.prompt: Read: « La transcription omet les hésitations de l'entretien ». What might change?
choices: Every recorded fact becomes false.
How the speaker's uncertainty or fluency is perceived.
The interview's publication year automatically.
questions.explanation: Removing hesitations may change perceived speech characteristics.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le rapport emploie le conditionnel pour rapporter une rumeur ». How should readers interpret it?
choices: As information not yet established.
As a certain first-hand observation.
As an imperative instruction.
questions.explanation: Conditional reporting can signal uncertainty and attribution.

questions.prompt: Read: « L'auteur utilise nous sans préciser son public ». What is unclear?
choices: Whether nous has a plural form.
Whether the word refers only to the future.
Who is included by the pronoun.
questions.explanation: The referent of nous affects group identity and claimed authority.

questions.prompt: Read: « Les sous-titres simplifient un terme culturel sans note ». What concern follows?
choices: The original must contain no cultural context.
A culturally specific distinction may be lost.
Subtitles cannot communicate any meaning.
questions.explanation: Simplification may erase cultural nuance when no note explains it.

questions.prompt: Read: « Une citation est détachée de sa réponse initiale ». What should be examined?
choices: The surrounding exchange and original question.
Only the font of the quoted phrase.
Whether the citation contains a long word.
questions.explanation: Dialogue context affects the meaning of a selected quotation.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le témoignage emploie un dialecte local dans l'enregistrement ». What principle is important?
choices: Correct every variety to one prestige accent without notice.
Assume every speaker shares the same dialect.
Describe the variety without treating it as defective French.
questions.explanation: Language varieties have social and historical contexts deserving respect.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le titre anglais est plus accusateur que le titre français ». What might this alter?
choices: Whether the article contains paragraphs.
The perceived stance of the publication.
The original date of the historical event.
questions.explanation: A more accusatory title can change perceived editorial framing.

questions.prompt: An archival source contains an offensive historical term. Which editorial action is responsible?
choices: Quote only as needed, contextualize it, and avoid adopting its viewpoint.
Erase the source's context and repeat the term as neutral.
Treat offensive wording as proof of objective description.
questions.explanation: Contextualized, limited quotation documents harmful language without endorsement.

questions.prompt: You find two translations of a politically important sentence. What should you do?
choices: Choose the one that best supports your conclusion without disclosure.
Combine both into a fabricated quotation.
Compare both with the source wording and explain differences.
questions.explanation: Translation comparisons require source checking and transparent explanation.

questions.prompt: An interview uses informal speech in French. Which transcription policy is best?
choices: Remove all signs of the speaker's language variety.
Preserve meaningful features and explain any normalization.
Silently rewrite every statement as formal literary prose.
questions.explanation: Transparent transcription protects speaker voice and documentary accuracy.

questions.prompt: A museum label describes one contested interpretation as universally accepted. Which revision is strongest?
choices: Cette interprétation est défendue par certains chercheurs, mais reste discutée.
Cette interprétation est vraie pour toujours et pour tous.
Toute autre interprétation est interdite.
questions.explanation: Attribution and the acknowledgment of debate improve scholarly accuracy.

questions.prompt: You translate « mémoire » in a discussion of collective history. What should guide the choice?
choices: Always use one English word regardless of context.
Replace the term with an unrelated modern slogan.
Its historical context and whether memory or remembrance is intended.
questions.explanation: Mémoire may require context-sensitive translation depending on its use.

questions.prompt: A documentary narrator claims to speak for a community. What should the analysis ask?
choices: Whether a formal voice guarantees community consent.
Whose voices are included and who authorized the representation?
Whether the narrator has the longest speaking time.
questions.explanation: Representation depends on whose perspectives are present and claimed authority.

questions.prompt: An edited historical letter uses square brackets to fill a missing name. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The bracketed text is an editorial addition, not original wording.
The bracketed text is always handwritten in the original.
The brackets prove the name was never uncertain.
questions.explanation: Scholarly brackets can distinguish editorial supplementation from source text.

questions.prompt: You must present an uncertain source attribution. Which French sentence fits?
choices: Cette autrice a forcément écrit le texte, sans source.
Aucune attribution n'a jamais besoin d'être justifiée.
Le texte est attribué à cette autrice, mais l'identification reste incertaine.
questions.explanation: Attribué à and reste incertaine preserve uncertainty about authorship.

questions.prompt: Your report quotes a witness after translating their words. Which note is most responsible?
choices: Citation incontestable parce que traduite.
Citation traduite; texte original et choix de traduction disponibles en annexe.
Citation originale, même si elle a été modifiée sans mention.
questions.explanation: Identifying translation and providing the source text allows critical review.
